correctness.rationale: Exact cofactor differentiation turns each linearized cube-facet determinant into an affine-interpolation minor. Complete Cauchy–Binet gives N^n times the orthogonal residual for N=2^(n-1); parity of the Walsh sectors eliminates all mixed terms; facet-degree counting yields (n-2)N^(n+1) and nN^(n+1). Dividing by 2^n yields the sharp two eigenvalues. For n=3 the higher band is absent. Direct Bareiss enumeration for n=3,4,5 yielded 15 passing exact determinant assertions, serving only as finite corroboration.

originality.rationale: The closest primary manuscript, arXiv:2606.14709v4, defines the identical operator and explicitly leaves its general Fourier coefficients unevaluated, giving only lambda_(3,2). The new claim calculates every value and the sharp least singular number. A different joint edge-length/planarity rigidity framework is not a dominating result. Related Walsh minor and sampling results were compared by object and implication; residual historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical result may have the same full-minor Gram calculation under an affine-regression, rigidity, or frame-theory formulation.

value.rationale: This computes the exact all-dimensional constants expressly left open in the principal rigidity theorem, with sharp stability and conditioning under a natural full-incidence norm. Quadratic Walsh modes are the uniquely least-sensitive nonhomothetic perturbations, and the condition number tends to one in high dimension. The result is a motivated geometric spectral refinement, not a renaming or arbitrary numerical slice; it does not assert nonlinear Mahler bounds.
